transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood Solutions), Dr. Alan Briggs, Maya Lopez, Jon Park, Sara Ito, Kevin Wu
Links shared: https://redwood.example.com/decks/regenmed-console (deck), https://sheets.redwood.example.com/benchmarks/regenmed-latency (benchmarks)

[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros before we dive — I'm Ethan from Redwood, AE, Priya's our SE who'll run the console walkthrough.
[00:10] Dr. Alan Briggs: Hi all, Alan here. Short on time today so keen to see the debug flow and how we'd use this in a regulated environment.
[00:18] Priya: Great. We'll cover tracing, request logs, error analysis, and a root-cause playbook. We'll also show fallback routing and how to tie traces back to customer requests in your SRE tools.
[00:30] Jon Park: Quick background: we're running regenmed-v1 internally through a mix of hosted APIs and in-house endpoints. Main pain is intermittent 500s and long tail latency that spikes under batch loads. We also need to confirm we can run private deploys into our V-P-C and keep keys in our KMS.
[00:50] Maya: And from an SRE perspective, we want clear playbooks — the team currently spends hours reproducing errors because request context is lost when we go through the gateway and a cascade of retries.
[01:05] Priya: Totally. We'll show request-id propagation, KV cache traces, and how to inspect prefix cache hits vs misses in the console.
[01:18] Ethan: Quick qual — what's your timeline for a pilot and who owns certification?
[01:22] Dr. Alan Briggs: We're targeting a Q4 pilot with a path to production early next year. Security will own certs but I want our infra and SRE leads to be comfortable first.
[01:33] Sara Ito: From security, SOC 2 and ISO are required; we also need SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs that show token-level access.
[01:45] Priya: We have a SOC2 package we can share. Console has audit trails per request, and our private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. We'll send the docs.
[01:56] [02:05] -- Demo portion starts -- Priya shares screen -- console logging view --
[02:10] Priya: Opening the 'Requests' view. You can search by request id, user id, model, or time range. Notice the left panel shows correlated traces — when a request hits the prefix cache, we annotate with 'cache:hit' and you can expand the KV entries.
[02:28] Kevin Wu: How granular is the KV info? We need to know if a cache was primed by a specific user prompt.
[02:34] Priya: You can see the exact prompt hash and the cache key, though for PII-sensitive apps we support redaction and hashed keys. The console shows the key name, TTL, and any eviction events in the timeline.
[02:48] [02:55] Speaker label glitch: shows Speaker 2 for Priya briefly
[03:00] Priya: Sorry, audio hiccup — back on track. Here's a sample 500 error. The top of the request shows the model variant, sequence length, and the kernel selection log — sometimes a mismatch in kernel causes OOM on a particular GPU profile.
[03:20] Jon Park: Wait, kernel selection? That's the runtime choosing optimized low-level kernels, right? Could that explain our sporadic OOMs when we hit longer sequences?
[03:27] Priya: Exactly — we log kernel selection and memory estimates. You can filter traces where 'kernel=amx-optimized' vs 'kernel=baseline' and correlate with failure rates.
[03:40] Maya: That would save so much debugging time. Right now we only see 500s in the gateway logs.
[03:46] Priya: We also have an 'error waterfall' feature in the console — aggregates errors by signature and shows sample stack-ish logs. Note that transcriptions of stack traces can be messy if your application strips characters, but we surface the key lines.
[04:01] Ethan: Can we map traces back to our SLOs? Like automatically flag requests above p95?
[04:07] Priya: Yes, there's a trace filter for latency buckets; you can create alerts for p50/p95/p99 thresholds and link them to runbook steps. We'll demo a rule-based alert linked to a playbook.
[04:22] [04:25] Demo: setting up an alert -> linking to runbook -> Slack + PagerDuty action shown
[04:40] Priya: Now watch a live playback — request 0f9a-... had a long tail. Playback replays token timing and external call events so you can see where the 200ms pause is introduced (in this case, a remote DB call causing blocking I/O).
[04:56] Jon Park: Nice. How does playback handle streaming responses?
[05:00] Priya: We reconstruct streaming chunks and timeline. For streaming failures we annotate chunk dropouts and show KV cache misses that might have forced recomputation.
[05:10] Kevin Wu: About sensitive content — will playback expose raw prompts?
[05:14] Priya: By default it's raw, but you can enable prompt redaction; we support allowlists for tokens and structural masking. For Private, you can enforce redaction at the ingress layer.
[05:25] [05:34] Transition to fallback routing demo
[05:36] Priya: Next, fallback routing: if a model variant hits a capacity spike or errors, our policy engine can route to a compatible quantized variant or to a cheaper CPU fallback. You can see per-request route decisions in the trace.
[05:50] Dr. Alan Briggs: For clinical workloads, we need deterministic behavior. How do you avoid quality regressions when fallback triggers?
[05:58] Priya: You can set a quality budget and enable canary evaluation — a sample of traffic is sent to the fallback and outputs are evaluated against golden prompt sets. If drift exceeds threshold, route is disabled. "Redwood Optimize" will recommend quantization profiles to minimize drift.
[06:20] Maya: That demo of canary validation is critical for us. We can't have silent regressions in inference outputs.
[06:28] Priya: Agreed. We'll share our evaluation harness and sample diff reports.
[06:34] [06:40] Pause, attendee background noise, muffled conversation in the background
[06:48] Priya: Back to traces — here's an incident where a retry loop caused amplification: the request retried at the gateway and spilled into the dedicated pool causing queueing. The trace shows retry headers and the client id; you can pivot to related requests to see the retry chain.
[07:05] Jon Park: Can we automatically collapse retries into a single logical request in the UI?
[07:09] Priya: Yes, enable request grouping by originating client id + original request id. That collapses the waterfall and attributes cost and latency correctly.
[07:20] Ethan: On the cost front — can we get token-level cost breakdowns per request? Our finance folks want per-feature cost allocation.
[07:29] Priya: The console gives token counts and cost estimates per request; you can tag routes and queries so that costs roll up to features. We also export CSV for billing reconciliation.
[07:40] Sara Ito: About compliance — what about audit log retention and exportability? For audits we need raw logs for 12 months with signer verification.
[07:48] Priya: We support configurable retention windows, S3 export, and signed audit logs. In Private, those logs can stay in your account or a dedicated bucket.
[07:59] [08:05] -- Deep-dive: kernel and memory trace example --
[08:08] Priya: Here's a trace where memory climbed and the runtime switched kernels mid-request. You can see the memory estimator warning recorded 500ms before OOM. We surface the estimated peak and the actual used memory.
[08:22] Kevin Wu: If estimator warned earlier, can we set preemptive throttling?
[08:26] Priya: Yes, policy rules can limit token emission rates or offload to a lower-memory variant. That can be automated or require human approval.
[08:36] Dr. Alan Briggs: How intrusive is the tracer on latency? Adding tracing can itself add overhead.
[08:42] Priya: We designed the tracing to be low overhead — sampling is configurable (1% to 100%), and playback is built from async logs so live latency impact is minimal.
[08:53] Maya: Good. Sampling will help.
[08:57] [09:05] -- Customer shares recent incident IDs for investigation --
[09:10] Maya: We pushed three failing request IDs into chat earlier: req-0f9a, req-3c4b, req-7ad1. Can you show how we'd triage those?
[09:20] Priya: Pulling up req-3c4b — you can see it hit a kernel mismatch and had a cache miss followed by a backend call to an on-prem db that timed out. The console shows the timeline: ingress -> KV miss -> runtime kernel load -> backend call -> timeout -> retry.
[09:36] Priya: If you click 'related requests' you see earlier warmup requests that primed the cache; it looks like the client ramp missed a priming call due to a 502 upstream.
[09:48] Jon Park: So it's a race between priming and traffic ramp — we can change our rollout to include warmup traffic.
[09:55] Priya: Exactly — the playbook step would be 'inject priming batch' followed by monitoring for cache hit ratio improvement.
[10:03] [10:10] Ethan: Let's talk about private deployment differences — what changes in traces when we run private?
[10:15] Priya: Most telemetry is the same; trace collection can be forwarded to your observability backends (Datadog/NewRelic) or kept in Redwood's console. The difference is where audit logs live and who controls the KMS.
[10:26] Sara Ito: For HIPAA-like workloads we need to ensure no plaintext logs leave our VPC. Is that supported?
[10:31] Priya: Yes, Private supports in-VPC storage, and we can run an on-prem package for air-gapped needs. We can also apply tokenization at ingress to avoid logging PHI.
[10:41] Dr. Alan Briggs: Any special network configs we should expect for VPC peering?
[10:46] Priya: We'll share a VPC checklist — egress rules, NAT, and peering options; for dedicated pools, we recommend private subnets with endpoint routing.
[10:55] [11:05] -- Walkthrough: Error analysis page --
[11:07] Priya: The 'Error analysis' page groups by signature and root cause tags. Our NLP-based clustering may mislabel some rare errors, so you can override tags. The page also suggests likely remediation steps like 'increase GPU mem', 'adjust batch size', 'switch quantized variant'.
[11:24] Maya: How accurate are the NLP suggestions? Last time we saw a false positive where a legit model output was flagged as a runtime error.
[11:32] Priya: We're improving the model — suggestions are scored and you can mark feedback to improve the classifier for your account.
[11:39] Jon Park: Can we onboard custom error signatures? We have domain-specific exceptions.
[11:44] Priya: Yes, you can upload rules and regexes for signature detection; those become first-class filters in the console.
[11:50] [11:58] -- Q&A and objection handling --
[12:00] Ethan: Common question — "why Redwood vs self-hosting?" Priya: Redwood reduces time to production and provides performance tuning, autoscaling, and unified tooling across hosted/dedicated/private. SE: plus our kernel and routing optimizations reduce token cost for median workloads.
[12:18] Dr. Alan Briggs: Our procurement will push back on vendor lock. If we go dedicated or private, how hard is it to migrate away?
[12:25] Ethan: We support export of models, your audit logs, and configuration bundles. Private is deployable in your infra so you maintain control.
[12:33] Sara Ito: What about encrypted key management and HSM?
[12:36] Priya: We integrate with AWS KMS, Google KMS, and custom HSM solutions for Private deployments. Keys never transit our control plane in Private mode.
[12:46] Maya: Competitor note: we've spoken to Anthropic and a cloud vendor; they lack a unified fallback + eval pipeline which is attractive in Redwood.
[12:56] Ethan: Understood. We'll include a competitive matrix.
[13:00] [13:05] -- Recap and next steps --
[13:08] Ethan: Recap: 1) We'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts and the VPC checklist. 2) Priya will upload the runbook and example trace queries. 3) We'll share pilot pricing and a recommended pilot plan for a 1-week scope to validate latency and cache priming. 4) RegenMed to share sample request IDs and stakeholder list.
[13:28] Dr. Alan Briggs: Sounds good. Target the kickoff week 10/27. We'll confirm security stakeholders by 10/21.
[13:36] Priya: I'll also include a short guide to configuring canary evaluation and how to set the quality budget to avoid silent regressions.
[13:43] Ethan: Final ask — can you run an initial benchmark using our regenmed-v1 prompt set?
[13:48] Jon Park: We'll provide the prompt set and expected p95 target.
[13:52] Ethan: Great. We'll follow up via email with links and the pricing attachment. Thanks everyone.
[13:57] [14:00] Call ends

Notes about transcript quality: occasional speaker mislabels, some proper nouns mangled (V-P-C appears as VPC/V-P-C), and short audio glitch at 06:34.
